rationale: The buyer's four stated priorities are, in order of emphasis in the company profile: (1) accurate multi-country payroll, (2) low admin effort, (3) integration with an existing HR system, (4) predictable pricing. BrightPay Cloud is the only vendor whose profile addresses all four with the greatest specificity and the fewest unmitigated gaps.

PRIORITY 1 – Accurate multi-country payroll: BrightPay Cloud handles UK PAYE/RTI and Irish PAYE/PRSI within a single tenant and, critically, is the only vendor whose profile explicitly includes a full audit log of every change and automated statutory filing to both HMRC and Revenue.ie. This directly de-risks late-filing penalties and supports the 'accurate' qualifier. Acme's Ireland module is characterised as secondary, and Cobalt's compliance/audit detail is not specified, making BrightPay the strongest on this dimension.

PRIORITY 2 – Low admin effort: BrightPay Cloud is the only vendor that quantifies the admin burden (<30 minutes of human intervention per cycle for 200 employees; <1 FTE benchmark) and describes an exception-based dashboard that surfaces only items needing manual review. Acme and Cobalt describe automation-first rules engines but provide no time-per-cycle figure. The one caveat is that BrightPay excludes native pension/benefits administration, which would add a small recurring admin step; however, this is a narrower gap than Acme's secondary-Ireland-module risk or Cobalt's unspecified SLA.

PRIORITY 3 – Integration with an existing HR system: All three vendors offer pre-built connectors for the same short list of common HRIS platforms (BambooHR, HiBob, Personio). BrightPay Cloud differentiates by specifying bi-directional sync of employee master data, leave balances, and org-chart changes, which most closely matches the buyer's need to avoid duplicate data entry. The shared risk across all three vendors is that a niche or legacy HR system would require custom API work; this is not a differentiator but a shared caveat the buyer must validate in a live RFP.

PRIORITY 4 – Predictable pricing: BrightPay Cloud is the strongest on this priority. Its profile explicitly states: no mid-term escalation within the 12-month contract, no per-run/per-filing/per-report transaction fees, a published add-on catalogue at fixed monthly rates, and a one-time onboarding fee. By contrast, Acme's assumed CPI + 2 % annual escalation clause and open-ended add-on costs (custom API, premium support, extra countries, analytics) introduce variability that partially erodes predictability. Cobalt is qualitatively similar to BrightPay but lacks a quantified escalation clause or PEPM range, leaving a minor ambiguity that BrightPay does not share.

WEIGHTED ASSESSMENT: Across the four priorities, BrightPay Cloud scores highest or tied-highest on three (multi-country accuracy, low admin effort, predictable pricing) and tied on the fourth (HR integration). Its principal weaknesses – geographic ceiling, connector-limited integration, no embedded pension admin, UK-hours-only support – are either shared by all three vendors (geographic ceiling, connector limitation) or are narrow, addressable gaps (pension admin via a separate provider; 24/7 support as a paid add-on). No single weakness in BrightPay's profile directly contradicts a stated buyer priority, whereas Acme's escalation clause and secondary-Ireland positioning, and Cobalt's unspecified SLA, each create a more material tension with the buyer's priorities.

CAVEAT: All three vendors are fictional. No real pricing sheet, SLA document, security certification, or product documentation exists for any of them. This recommendation is an illustrative exercise only. Before any live procurement, the buyer must (a) issue a formal RFP to real vendors, (b) obtain written quotes itemising PEPM rate, onboarding fee, integration-build cost, and escalation clause, (c) verify ISO 27001 / SOC 2 or equivalent security certifications, (d) confirm that the buyer's specific existing HR system is on the vendor's pre-built connector list, and (e) validate the 24/7 support add-on cost if Irish filing deadlines fall outside UK business hours.

- Assumed model: Per-employee-per-month (PEPM) subscription, billed annually. A plausible mid-market band for a 200-employee UK+Ireland deployment might be in the range of £12–£22 PEPM, but this figure is INVENTED for illustration and has no basis in any real product.

- Assumed exclusions / potential add-ons: custom API integration (one-off project fee), premium/24-7 support tier, additional countries beyond UK/Ireland, and advanced analytics dashboards. These would introduce variable costs that partially erode the 'predictable pricing' priority.

strengths: Multi-country payroll (UK + Ireland): BrightPay Cloud is positioned as a UK/Ireland-focused SaaS payroll provider. For a 200-employee company with staff in both jurisdictions, it natively handles UK PAYE/RTI and Irish PAYE/PRSI filing within a single tenant, eliminating the need for two separate systems. (Assumption: the fictional vendor's documented coverage is limited to these two countries; no broader EU or US modules are claimed.)

Low admin effort: The platform is fully cloud-hosted with automated tax-rule updates (HMRC and Revenue.ie schedules pushed centrally), in-year corrections, and year-end reporting (P60/P45, P60 equivalents for Ireland). A 200-employee payroll can typically be run in under 30 minutes of human intervention per cycle, with exception-based dashboards flagging only items that need manual review. (Assumption: 'low admin' is defined as <1 FTE for a 200-head payroll; this is a reasonable mid-market benchmark but is not a verified figure for a fictional product.)

HR-system integration: BrightPay Cloud exposes a REST API and pre-built connectors for a short list of common HRIS/HRM platforms (e.g., BambooHR, Personio, HiBob). For a company that already runs an HR system, bi-directional sync of employee master data, leave balances, and org-chart changes reduces duplicate data entry. (Assumption: the buyer's 'existing HR system' is one of the listed connectors; if it is a bespoke or niche system, integration would require custom API work, which is not included in the base product.)

Predictable pricing: The vendor publishes a per-employee-per-month (PEPM) subscription with a fixed annual contract, no per-run or per-filing transaction fees, and a published add-on catalogue. This aligns directly with the buyer's 'predictable pricing' priority. (Assumption: 'predictable' means no hidden per-transaction charges; annual contracts lock the rate for 12 months.)

Compliance and audit trail: Automated statutory filing to HMRC (RTI) and Revenue.ie, with a full audit log of every change, supports the 'accurate multi-country payroll' priority and reduces the risk of late-filing penalties.
weaknesses: Geographic ceiling: BrightPay Cloud's documented coverage is UK and Ireland only. If the 200-employee company later expands into the EU, US, or APAC, a second or third payroll system would be required, creating the multi-vendor complexity the buyer is trying to avoid. (Assumption: no roadmap for additional countries is published for this fictional vendor.)

Integration depth is connector-limited: Pre-built connectors cover a handful of popular HRIS platforms. If the buyer's existing HR system is not on that list, integration falls back to a generic REST API that requires in-house or third-party development effort, partially negating the 'low admin effort' benefit. (Assumption: custom integration is billed as a professional-services line item, not included in the PEPM fee.)

Limited self-service for employees: The employee portal (payslip access, P45/P60 download, tax-code changes) is functional but less polished than consumer-grade apps; it may not meet expectations of a 200-person workforce accustomed to modern UX, potentially generating support tickets that add to admin load.

Support model: Standard support is email + phone during UK business hours (Mon–Fri, 09:00–17:00 GMT). There is no 24/7 or on-call option in the base tier, which could be a gap for a company with Irish staff whose filing deadlines fall outside UK hours. (Assumption: premium 24/7 support is available as a paid add-on.)

No embedded benefits or pension administration: BrightPay Cloud handles gross-to-net payroll and statutory filings but does not include pension auto-enrolment administration (UK) or PRSI-linked pension schemes (Ireland) as a native module; the buyer would need a separate benefits/pension provider, adding a small integration and admin overhead.

weaknesses: Geographic ceiling: The profile is scoped to UK and Ireland.
